beforeReviewCorrections.why: the same two texts measured before the code-review corrections of PR #902 (quotations spanning a wrapped line, table header rows skipped, a path written with lines and alone checked for both, bare js/ts/in names only in code marks or with lines)

reading: Before and after the review corrections: the plain synthesis goes from 103 to 101 claims (its 2 table header rows are no longer claims) and from one verified claim of 2 to 1 verified and 1 quotation-not-found. The claim at plain-synthesis.txt lines 136-139 wraps a quotation across a line; before the correction the line-bound reader paired the closing quote of one quotation with the opening quote of the next and verified the span ' and ' it found between them; now it reads the two written quotations, and neither is a contiguous span of the files the claim names. The dossier arm is unchanged in every count.

The plain synthesis names 127 file references (128 before the corrections, one of them a bare js name in prose) and attaches lines to none; the dossier text names 336, 180 with lines, all 180 resolving at the pinned revision.

Quotations: the plain synthesis has 4 double-quoted spans: 1 verified in a whole file its claim names, 2 not found, 1 in a claim naming no file. The dossier text shows none checked, because scripts/dossier_site_to_text.py drops the quotation marks around the 9 lead-in quotations the dossier renders ('The project states:'), so the dossier arm is under-counted on quotations.

path-missing in the dossier arm (17 references) is mostly the dossier naming its own pages (index.html, poles/1.html and the like) and generator files that are not in the repository; in the plain arm (2) a configuration file and a header that resolve to no blob.
A bare or partial name resolves to the one blob whose path ends with it; an ambiguous one stays missing.

unanchored counts claims naming no file: 33 of 101 plain claims and 397 of 689 dossier claims (the dossier text includes navigation lists, glossary entries and labels). The checker measures whether a claim can be checked and whether its quotation is real, not whether an unquoted claim is true.

The pilot's stored run is a legacy polaris-dossier-run/1 record that `syzygy dossier verify` refuses to re-verify, so this measurement used the script over the pilot manifest; both call the same verifyText.
